decisions.reason: The evening day-patient program uses the existing psychiatric infrastructure and insurer reimbursement, so keeping it open costs little while demand from working patients is still becoming clear.
The carpentry workshop runs on sheltered-workshop capacity and gives meaningful work, so it is cheap to keep even though its commercial value is still uncertain after the retail shop was dropped.
Outpatient sociotherapy fits the core psychiatric care business and is reimbursed, so waiting for its uptake to show is worth more than abandoning it.
Senior living counseling is prominent, cheap to run and feeds demand into the core eldercare business, so its value is already largely evident.
The newly launched meal delivery service is close to existing kitchen and eldercare operations, and its uncertainty is still high, so it is worth keeping open at modest cost.
